sentiment.rationale: The document shows a genuine operational inflection: Boeing swung from a GAAP operating loss of ($10,707M) in FY2024 to a profit of $4,281M in FY2025, and from negative free cash flow of ($14.3B) to a usage of only ($1.9B). Commercial deliveries more than doubled year-over-year (348 to 600), and management provided explicit positive free cash flow guidance of $1B-$3B for FY2026, a material improvement from the prior year's cash burn. However, the score is capped at +0.25 because the improvement is partly attributed to a one-time $9.6B gain on the Digital Aviation Solutions divestiture, and the document also discloses a new $565M charge on the KC-46A tanker program and ongoing structural risks on fixed-price development programs and certification delays.

summary.revenue: FY2025 revenue of $89,463M, up 34% from $66,517M in FY2024. Q4 2025 revenue of $23,948M, up 57% from $15,242M in Q4 2024.
summary.eps: FY2025 GAAP diluted EPS of $2.48, compared to a loss of ($18.36) in FY2024. FY2025 Core EPS (non-GAAP) of $1.19, compared to a loss of ($20.38) in FY2024.
summary.guidance: Management guided FY2026 free cash flow of $1B-$3B, a material improvement from FY2025's ($1.9B) usage. BCA deliveries expected to be up ~10% year-over-year, with 737 deliveries around 500 aircraft and 787 deliveries between 90-100 aircraft. Management stated the $10B free cash flow mark is 'very attainable' over time.
summary.margin: FY2025 GAAP operating margin of 4.8%, compared to (16.1)% in FY2024. Core operating margin (non-GAAP) of 3.6%, compared to (17.8)% in FY2024. Q4 2025 GAAP operating margin of 36.7% (includes $9.6B gain on DAS sale), compared to (24.7)% in Q4 2024.
key_risks: New $565M charge on KC-46A tanker program driven by higher production support and supply chain costs.
Ongoing certification delays on 777X, 737-7, and 737-10 programs.
Potential durability issue identified on 777X engine requiring root cause and corrective action.
Structural risk on fixed-price development programs (KC-46A, Commercial Crew, VC-25B, T-7A, MQ-25) with potential for additional reach-forward losses.
Tariff and trade policy uncertainty, particularly with China and Europe.
Approximately $1B unfavorable cash flow impact from Spirit AeroSystems integration in FY2026.
DOJ payment of $445M sliding from 2025 to 2026.
key_opportunities: Record total company backlog of $682B, including record BCA backlog of $567B with over 6,100 airplanes.
Record BDS backlog of $85B and record BGS backlog of $30B.
Planned production rate increases: 737 from 42 to 47/month in 2026, 787 targeting 10/month later in 2026.
New 737 production line in Everett (North Line) with facility and tooling investments complete.
BDS secured transformational win for U.S. Air Force sixth-generation fighter (F-47).
BGS delivered 6% organic growth and 18%+ margins in 2025.
Management stated $10B free cash flow is 'very attainable' over time.

management_tone.label: confident
management_tone.justification: Management described the year as setting 'the foundation for our turnaround' and stated the $10B free cash flow mark is 'very attainable,' while acknowledging remaining work: 'We haven't fully turned the corner, but we're making real progress.'

review_flags.reason: The score of +0.25 reflects genuine operational momentum and a guidance raise (FCF guidance of $1B-$3B), but the improvement is heavily influenced by a one-time $9.6B gain. A reviewer should confirm the weighting between organic improvement and one-time items is appropriate.

The DOJ payment of $445M is listed as a risk, but it was already accrued in FY2025 results; the cash outflow in FY2026 is a timing item, not a new risk. A reviewer may wish to reclassify or clarify this.
